Diego to run 48h throughput + latency benchmark on proposed dedicated pool and share results by 2026-06-03
Sofia to upload SOC2 scope and confirm data residency constraints by 2026-06-02
Schedule security deep-dive (Redwood SE + Magellan Sec team) week of 2026-06-07

Avery — send term-extension pricing and SOW; due 2026-05-30

summary: Check-in to confirm Magellan's capacity uplift for upcoming Q4 peak, discuss adding APAC region (Singapore), and finalize a one-year term extension with reserved dedicated capacity. Security concerns (SOC2, KMS, data residency) raised; agreed to run benchmarks and a security deep-dive.
topics: Capacity uplift for ad-serving peak windows
APAC region onboarding (Singapore) and replication lag concerns
Contract term extension and committed reserved capacity pricing
Private/VPC deployment vs hosted dedicated tradeoffs
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-27; Start: 14:00 PT; Duration: ~48 minutes; Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (VP Eng - Magellan), Liam O'Connor (Platform Lead), Sofia Tran (Security & Compliance)

[00:00] Avery: Hey all, thanks for making time, uh we'll do a quick agenda — capacity bump, APAC region onboarding, and the term extension pricing. quick check — everyone's good to chat?
[00:12] Priya: Yep, hi, thanks. we have about 10 folks but this is the core group.
[00:18] Liam: Morning from Dublin — yes, ready.
[00:22] Diego: Hi, Diego here. I'll run through the perf questions and benchmark plan.
[00:27] Sofia: Sofia here for security questions, mainly SOC2 and data residency.

[00:40] Avery: Cool. Priya can you give us a quick refresher on the runway — what's changed since we last touched base? like traffic delta, timeline for Q4?
[00:48] Priya: Sure. So since our last check in growth has been faster than forecast — about 35% qtr-over-qtr for ad impressions, and we now expect a clear Q4 peak where peak qps could be 2.2x current steady state. so we want to lock in reserved capacity earlier to avoid cold starts and bidding delays.
[01:10] Liam: And just to add — our p95 latency target for auctions is sub-120ms. p50 is fine right now but the tail is what kills ctr and revenue.
[01:20] Avery: Understood. Diego, from a serving perspective, rough guidance on how much headroom to reserve?
[01:28] Diego: From the numbers they gave, my back-of-envelope says we should consider a 2.5x dedicated pool for peak with autoscale headroom. But we should do a workload-specific bench — token sizes here are small, but the real cost is concurrency. We'll propose a dedicated instance config tuned for short-seq attention and KV cache warmup.
[01:46] Priya: Quick question — is KV cache persisted across restarts? last time we saw longer warm ups during a brigade of deploys. sometimes the KV cash — sorry, cache — warming is a thing.
[01:58] Diego: Good call — current Redwood dedicated supports prefix/KV caching with warm-start; but, uh, depending on how you deploy, there can be some cold periods. we'll show mitigation: staggered rolling restarts and warm replicas. also we can pin model versions to avoid unexpected cold re-compiles.
[02:18] Sofia: On the security note, we need to confirm encryption at rest keys — we need customer-managed keys (KMS) and assurances on who can rotate them. also SSO/SAML integration is required for our ops team and RBAC for route-level permissions.
[02:34] Avery: Yep, we can support KMS integration and SAML SSO. Diego — can you capture the details on RBAC granularity?
[02:41] Diego: We have role scoping for project, route and model. It's not, like, as granular as custom lambda policies out of the box but we'll map to your org roles. we'll also show audit logs per request for compliance.
[02:54] Liam: Audit logs — do they include token-level cost breakdown? that's important for chargeback internally.
[03:00] Avery: Yes, Redwood Console gives token cost + latency per token breakdown. we'll include sample screenshots in the SOW.
[03:06] Priya: Great. Back to regions — we want APAC, specifically Singapore, to reduce RTT for DSP integrations in APAC. we also may need EU edge for GDPR sensitive advertisers.
[03:19] Diego: Singapore region is supported on dedicated; latency typically drops 40-60ms for APAC. there's also replication lag if you have global KV cache, but we can do regional isolated caches or async replication depending on consistency needs.
[03:34] Priya: For auctions a few ms of staleness is acceptable, but the concern is write through and immediate read for bidder state. so we want to confirm strong read-after-write for route-level state.
[03:48] Diego: In that case regional isolated caches with a write-forwarding pattern will be better; there is a small tradeoff in cost but it preserves strong reads for local traffic.
[03:58] Sofia: Also need to confirm data residency — certain advertiser buckets must not leave Singapore or EU. can Redwood guarantee region-locking of those request payloads?
[04:08] Avery: Yes, Private/VPC deployment gives that level of isolation. Hosted dedicated also supports region locking for storage — we'll include specifics. Diego, maybe call out the options: hosted dedicated with region lock vs private VPC on customer infra.
[04:22] Diego: Hosted dedicated with region-lock works for most setups; Private gives you full control — network policies, HSM integration for keys if you need. the on-prem package is available but it's heavier ops.
[04:34] Liam: Ops preference is managed hosted if we get the guarantees, because we don't want to run inference stacks ourselves. but we might need HSM for certain buckets; do you support external HSM?
[04:45] Avery: We integrate with customer KMS and HSM via standard connectors; Diego will share a matrix of supported KMS providers.
[04:53] Priya: On pricing, we'd like to negotiate a 12-month extension with committed reserved units and some ramp credits for the first two months of the new term. last time you offered ramp credits for new capacity before.
[05:06] Avery: Yep, historically we do a ramp credit tied to usage; for a 12-month commitment we can do a tiered credit structure. Diego, rough elasticity on pricing with 1yr commit?
[05:16] Diego: Typical structure: the bigger the reserved pool and longer the commit, the better discount. also adding multiple regions changes unit economics a bit; we'll show a blended rate with APAC premium.
[05:29] Priya: Can you send a sample SOW with the APAC add-on and the credit schedule?
[05:33] Avery: Absolutely, sending by Friday EOD.
[05:36] Liam: For the benchmark — we want to replicate our bidding workload which is a high QPS, small payload, 150 token-ish per request. can you run a 48-hour bench that simulates bursts?
[05:49] Diego: Yes, we'll run 48h — steady followed by modeled peak bursts. we'll include p50/p90/p95 latency and tail latencies under load. also will test failover and warm-up characteristics.
[05:59] Priya: Important that test includes cold start scenario and rolling deploys; our release cadence can cause a dozen deploys per day.
[06:06] Diego: we'll include both warm and cold start scenarios.
[06:09] Sofia: A few security follow-ups — PCI scope isn't in this project but advertiser PII has to be handled. we need SOC2 Type II report and penetration test cadence. also are request payloads redacted in logs by default?
[06:21] Avery: Logs can be configured to mask fields; default retention is X days but we can match enterprise retention on paid plans. SOC2 Type II is available; we'll share the cert and the controls.
[06:32] Sofia: Perfect. Also need evidence of quarterly pen tests and a contact for incident response.
[06:38] Avery: We'll share IR contacts and penetration test cadence.
[06:41] Priya: Timeline question — we want APAC on by mid-August to start the DSP integration POC. is that realistic?
[06:50] Diego: Realistic if we sign SOW by end of June. provisioning + validation + two-week pilot = ~6 weeks. so yes, mid-August is doable.
[06:59] Priya: Okay, so signing target end of June.
[07:03] Avery: Great. Let's cover any outstanding blockers — Liam?
[07:06] Liam: Need clarity on per-route RBAC and whether the token-level chargeback can be surfaced to our billing system as a CSV export.
[07:15] Avery: We can export token-level cost and usage via CSV or S3 export. Diego will include an example.
[07:22] Sofia: Also need confirmation that logs containing ad IDs are hashed/encrypted at rest and that any backups remain in-region for those buckets.
[07:32] Diego: Yes, bucket-level encryption and region-locking for backups is supported; will include config examples.
[07:40] Priya: What about SLA — last SLA offered was 99.9% for dedicated with credits. our procurement may push for a 99.95 target. is that on the table?
[07:51] Avery: 99.95 is possible for certain dedicated tiers with additional redundancy and zones; we'll map options in the SOW and the cost delta.
[07:59] Priya: Sounds good.
[08:02] [Pause — note: discussion moves into finer details, some crosstalk as attendees check docs]
[08:18] Diego: Quick note on model variants — you mentioned short sequences, we recommend quantized variant Q4 for cost efficiency, but if you need absolute tail latency lower, we can run non-quantized for dedicated hot paths.
[08:33] Priya: Keep both options, we may route critical auctions to hot path.
[08:38] Diego: Also planning for model pinning and canary routes so you don't get surprise regressions.
[08:44] Priya: Good.
[08:47] Avery: Ok I want to recap next steps: I'll send SOW + pricing with APAC add-on and ramp credit options by 2026-05-30. Diego will run 48h bench and share results by 2026-06-03. Sofia will provide SOC2 scope & residency details by 2026-06-02. Liam will give traffic profile by 2026-05-29. We tentatively target SOW signature end of June and APAC provisioning mid-August. Anything to add?
[09:14] Sofia: Can you also include an HSM/KMS integration checklist in the security doc?
[09:19] Diego: Yep will do.
[09:21] Priya: No, that's it. thanks.
[09:24] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and book the security deep-dive.
[09:30] Liam: Thanks all.
[09:32] [Call ends — total ~48 minutes]

Notes/Artifacts mentioned: SOW template link (shared via email), benchmark spreadsheet (to be populated), security pack (SOC2, pen test, KMS matrix).

Transcript quality notes: some words mis-transcribed (KV cash -> KV cache), minor speaker id swaps possible due to phone dial-ins.

Recap (verbatim style): 
- Magellan requests 2.5x headroom dedicated pool with autoscale and APAC (Singapore) region added.
- Security pre-reqs: SOC2 Type II, KMS/HSM integration, RBAC per-route, audit logs, in-region backups.
- Benchmarks: Redwood to run 48h throughput + peak burst tests including cold-starts and rolling deploys.
- Commercial: 12-month term extension with reserved units, ramp credits for first two months; Redwood to send SOW + pricing by 2026-05-30.

End of transcript.
